newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA TO SWAP WHEAT FOR GERMAN COMBINE HARVESTERS.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA TO SWAP WHEAT FOR GERMAN COMBINE HARVESTERS.

text.p: Bulgaria's cabinet on Thursday approved a futures contract to import eight combine harvesters from Germany against export of 5,000 tonnes of wheat from this year's crop, a government spokeswoman said.

"The interim cabinet increased the current quota for wheat export under futures contracts by 5,000 tonnes to 40,000 tonnes to pay for import of eight combine harvesters from Germany," the official told reporters.
In February the interim government approved export of 35,000 tonnes of wheat from this year's crop against imports of farm machines needed to improve the capacity of Bulgaria's outdated machinery.
Excessive wheat exports two years ago and a bad harvest last year led to acute grain and bread shortages earlier this year, which have been overcome in the past two months.
The IMF disbursed a $147 million loan to Bulgaria on Thursday to pay for grain imports. -- Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
